results.quote: There is a poset selection algorithm using O(k+OPT(G,k)) comparisons for each input (G,k,≺).
There is a poset selection algorithm using O(OPT(G,k)·log(k/OPT(G,k))) comparisons for each input (G,k,≺) when G is a rooted forest and OPT(G,k)≤1/2 k.

There is a poset selection algorithm using O(OPT(G,k)·loglog(k/OPT(G,k))) comparisons for each input (G,k,≺) when G is a rooted forest where each node of depth less than k has at least one child, and OPT(G,k)≤1/4 k. Alternatively, the number of comparisons can be bounded by O(OPT(G,k)logOPT(G,k)).

results.bound: O(w \cdot \log(1/\varepsilon)) \text{ for delete, } O(1) \text{ for all other operations}
results.quote: Weighted soft heaps can be implemented with amortized time O(w·log(1/ε)) for delete, where w is the weight of the deleted element, and O(1) amortized time for all other operations. The amortized number of comparisons performed by increase-weight is zero.

results.bound: O(k + OPT(P,k)) \text{ comparisons and } O(k + OPT(P,k) + e^*) \text{ time}
results.quote: There exists an algorithm for poset selection that takes O(k+OPT(P,k)) comparisons and O(k+OPT(P,k)+e*) time for each instance (P,k), where e* is the number of edges incident to some prefix of P of size O(k+OPT(P,k)).
For each forest F on n nodes and k∈[n], we have OPT(F,k)≥1/2 c*(F,k-1)-1.
Let k,k'∈N+ with k'<k and let F be a k-unbounded forest. Let m=c*(T,k'). Then OPT(F,k)≥Ω(m log((k-k')/m)).
